newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight steady as market stays tight.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight steady as market stays tight.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was steady at 8.4/6 percent as the market remained tight ahead of the long weekend, dealers said on Thursday.
They said with Bank Negara announcing plans to roll over a maturing 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bill next Wednesday, the market was expected to remain tight.
"This should keep interest rates firm for most of next week," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
The Malaysian money market is closed on Saturday for the Moslem Eid al-Adha celebrations.
Earlier, other interbank rates were also mostly steady after recent gains as the market continued to be short of funds.
One-week money ended the morning at 8.10/20 percent against 7.80/90 percent, while two-week at 7.50/60 percent and three-week at 7.35/40 percent were unchanged from Wednesday.
One-month to six-month money traded between 7.35 and 7.45 percent and nine-month and one-year rose to 7.45/48 percent against 7.40/45, the dealers said.
"Apart from the maturity, there is no new factor to change the market's trend," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
The market tightened on Wednesday after an outflow of 500 million ringgit due to a Bank Negara bill.
The outflow coupled with a steady draining of foreign funds from Malaysia had tightened the market and pushed up rates, dealers said.
Dealers said there was market talk that foreign funds were withdrawing from Malaysia, both from deposits and from the stock market, which has been falling sharply recently.
Last week, Bank Negara intervened to slow the ringgit's fall by selling nearly $200 million, dealers said. A 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue also reduced liquidity in the flush market.
Some dealers said there was also a persistent rumour about a possible long-term government bond issue soon, which would mop up further liquidity and roll over maturing bonds.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were steady across the board in late afternoon trading, but volumes dropped by more than half over previous sessions.
At 0800 GMT, three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate-based (KLIBOR) June contract was steady at 92.68, or an implied yield of 7.32 percent.
September was at 92.67, or 7.33 percent and December was down one point at 92.60, or 7.40 percent.
March 1998 contract was up one at 92.50.
